rows.title: Laplace-Smoothing Error Identity

maturity_record.invariant: For a positive finite sample, add-one smoothing decomposes forecast error into contracted empirical error plus an exact target-dependent offset.
maturity_record.assumption_review: The success count and sample count are natural numbers, sample count is positive, successes do not exceed it, and the target lies in the unit interval. The theorem is an algebraic identity, not a stochastic consistency or posterior-contraction result.
maturity_record.non_vacuity: The shrinkage coefficient lies in the unit interval and the separate boundary witness in fep-122 shows that the offset can be nonzero.
maturity_record.acceptance_probe: warning-free native Lean compile of fep121_laplaceError_identity and fep121_shrinkage_mem_unitInterval with the positive-sample premises.

qualified_declaration_statements.fep121_laplaceError_identity:
theorem fep121_laplaceError_identity
    (successes sampleCount : ℕ) (target : ℝ)
    (sampleCountPositive : 0 < sampleCount)
    (successesAtMost : successes ≤ sampleCount)
    (targetBounds : target ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) :
    laplaceEstimate successes sampleCount - target =
      shrinkage sampleCount * (empiricalRate successes sampleCount - target) +
        laplaceBias sampleCount target
qualified_declaration_statements.fep121_shrinkage_mem_unitInterval:
theorem fep121_shrinkage_mem_unitInterval (sampleCount : ℕ) :
    shrinkage sampleCount ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1

rows.statement_review: The add-one forecast error is exactly n/(n+2) times the raw empirical error plus(1-2*target)/(n+2). The row keeps admissible counts/target; the foundation identity actually only needs n>0.
rows.assumptions_and_scope: The offset is deterministic target-dependent smoothing bias, not automatically statistical bias. At n>0 shrinkage is strictly between0 and1, but the nonzero offset can increase error. Existing Dirichlet/Pólya count-level normalization and binary Laplace specialization already connect this expression to count updates.

maturity_record.invariant: The absolute target-dependent Laplace offset is at most one pseudo-count divided by the smoothed sample size.
maturity_record.assumption_review: The target is confined to the closed unit interval. The bound controls the deterministic smoothing offset and does not identify statistical bias under an unspecified sampling distribution.
maturity_record.non_vacuity: At sample count two and target zero, the offset equals one quarter and is explicitly nonzero.

rows.title: Absolute-Error Transfer through Laplace Smoothing

maturity_record.invariant: An absolute empirical-error certificate transfers through add-one smoothing with the exact shrinkage coefficient and one-pseudo-count offset.
maturity_record.assumption_review: Sample count is positive, successes are bounded by it, the target is in the unit interval, and the raw empirical error already has a supplied bound. No probability tail rate is inferred in this row.
maturity_record.non_vacuity: The source error may be positive and the smoothing offset remains visible; the theorem also proves that any supplied error upper bound is nonnegative.

qualified_declaration_statements.fep123_laplaceAbsoluteError_le:
theorem fep123_laplaceAbsoluteError_le
    (successes sampleCount : ℕ) (target error : ℝ)
    (sampleCountPositive : 0 < sampleCount)
    (successesAtMost : successes ≤ sampleCount)
    (targetBounds : target ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1)
    (empiricalErrorBound :
      |empiricalRate successes sampleCount - target| ≤ error) :
    |laplaceEstimate successes sampleCount - target| ≤
      shrinkage sampleCount * error + 1 / ((sampleCount : ℝ) + 2)
qualified_declaration_statements.fep123_error_nonnegative:
theorem fep123_error_nonnegative
    (successes sampleCount : ℕ) (target error : ℝ)
    (empiricalErrorBound :
      |empiricalRate successes sampleCount - target| ≤ error) :
    0 ≤ error

rows.title: Squared-Risk Transfer through Laplace Smoothing

maturity_record.invariant: Squared add-one error is bounded pointwise by twice the contracted empirical squared error plus twice the squared pseudo-count offset, and the inequality integrates under every normalized finite sampling law.
maturity_record.assumption_review: Sample count is positive, each success count is bounded by it, and the target is in the unit interval. The factor-two inequality is conservative and finite-law expectation is not an asymptotic risk claim.
maturity_record.non_vacuity: Nonzero empirical error and nonzero boundary offset both contribute to the integrated upper bound under a nondegenerate finite sampling law.
maturity_record.acceptance_probe: warning-free native Lean compile of fep124_laplaceSquaredError_le and fep124_laplaceSquaredRisk_le.

qualified_declaration_statements.fep124_laplaceSquaredError_le:
theorem fep124_laplaceSquaredError_le
    (successes sampleCount : ℕ) (target : ℝ)
    (sampleCountPositive : 0 < sampleCount)
    (successesAtMost : successes ≤ sampleCount)
    (targetBounds : target ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) :
    (laplaceEstimate successes sampleCount - target) ^ 2 ≤
      2 * shrinkage sampleCount ^ 2 *
          (empiricalRate successes sampleCount - target) ^ 2 +
        2 * (1 / ((sampleCount : ℝ) + 2)) ^ 2
qualified_declaration_statements.fep124_laplaceSquaredRisk_le:
theorem fep124_laplaceSquaredRisk_le
    {Ω : Type*} [Fintype Ω] (sampling : FiniteLaw Ω)
    (successes : Ω → ℕ) (sampleCount : ℕ) (target : ℝ)
    (sampleCountPositive : 0 < sampleCount)
    (successesAtMost : ∀ outcome, successes outcome ≤ sampleCount)
    (targetBounds : target ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) :
    FEP.VariationalDuality.expectation sampling (fun outcome =>
      (laplaceEstimate (successes outcome) sampleCount - target) ^ 2) ≤
      2 * shrinkage sampleCount ^ 2 *
          FEP.VariationalDuality.expectation sampling (fun outcome =>
            (empiricalRate (successes outcome) sampleCount - target) ^ 2) +
        2 * (1 / ((sampleCount : ℝ) + 2)) ^ 2

rows.assumptions_and_scope: Factor2 comes from(a+b)^2<=2a^2+2b^2; it does not certify risk decreases or a sharp variance/bias decomposition. Sampling need not be IID/binomial or generated by the target; success-count/target admissibility alone supplies no generalization claim.

rows.title: Bernoulli Brier Excess-Risk Identity

maturity_record.invariant: Bernoulli Brier excess risk relative to the true probability is exactly the squared forecast error.
maturity_record.assumption_review: The identity is polynomial and therefore holds over real target and forecast inputs; the probability interpretation requires both to lie in the unit interval, which is supplied by downstream statistical uses.
maturity_record.non_vacuity: A forecast unequal to the target has positive squared excess, while the self-forecast boundary has exactly zero excess.

qualified_declaration_statements.fep125_brierExcess_eq_sqError:
theorem fep125_brierExcess_eq_sqError (target forecast : ℝ) :
    bernoulliBrierScore target forecast - bernoulliBrierScore target target =
      (forecast - target) ^ 2
qualified_declaration_statements.fep125_brierExcess_self:
theorem fep125_brierExcess_self (target : ℝ) :
    bernoulliBrierScore target target - bernoulliBrierScore target target = 0

rows.statement_review: The defined Bernoulli quadratic score minus its value at forecast=target equals squared forecast error for all real inputs. This proves nonnegative excess and equality iff forecast=target algebraically.
rows.assumptions_and_scope: A Bernoulli probability/forecast interpretation requires unit-interval inputs; outside it the polynomial still holds but is not an expectation under a Bernoulli law. This does not establish frequency calibration or empirical skill.

rows.adverse_witness_specification_unexecuted: Target2 satisfies the polynomial but is not a Bernoulli parameter. Forecasts or losses do not by themselves demonstrate observed calibration.

qualified_declaration_statements.fep126_laplaceBrierRisk_le:
theorem fep126_laplaceBrierRisk_le
    {Ω : Type*} [Fintype Ω] (sampling : FiniteLaw Ω)
    (successes : Ω → ℕ) (sampleCount : ℕ) (target : ℝ)
    (sampleCountPositive : 0 < sampleCount)
    (successesAtMost : ∀ outcome, successes outcome ≤ sampleCount)
    (targetBounds : target ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) :
    brierExcessRisk sampling
        (fun outcome => laplaceEstimate (successes outcome) sampleCount) target ≤
      2 * shrinkage sampleCount ^ 2 *
          FEP.VariationalDuality.expectation sampling (fun outcome =>
            (empiricalRate (successes outcome) sampleCount - target) ^ 2) +
        2 * (1 / ((sampleCount : ℝ) + 2)) ^ 2

theorem fep126_sampling_mass_one
    {Ω : Type*} [Fintype Ω] (sampling : FiniteLaw Ω) :

rows.title: Concentration-Event Transfer through Smoothing

maturity_record.invariant: A smoothed deviation beyond the transferred threshold is contained in the corresponding raw empirical-deviation event, so any supplied finite-law probability bound transfers monotonically.
maturity_record.assumption_review: Sample count is positive, success counts are bounded, the target is in the unit interval, and a raw event-probability bound is supplied. The theorem composes with concentration results but does not derive their assumptions or rates itself.
maturity_record.non_vacuity: The smoothed and raw events are distinct whenever the shrinkage and offset change the threshold, and the finite-law monotonicity result applies to any nonzero failure bound.

    (sampleCountPositive : 0 < sampleCount)
    (successesAtMost : ∀ outcome, successes outcome ≤ sampleCount)
    (targetBounds : target ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) :
    laplaceBadEvent successes sampleCount target error ⊆
      empiricalBadEvent successes sampleCount target error
qualified_declaration_statements.fep127_laplaceBadEvent_probability_le:
theorem fep127_laplaceBadEvent_probability_le
    {Ω : Type*} [Fintype Ω] (sampling : FiniteLaw Ω)
    (successes : Ω → ℕ) (sampleCount : ℕ)
    (target error failure : ℝ)
    (sampleCountPositive : 0 < sampleCount)
    (successesAtMost : ∀ outcome, successes outcome ≤ sampleCount)
    (targetBounds : target ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1)
    (rawProbabilityBound :
      finiteEventProbability sampling
        (empiricalBadEvent successes sampleCount target error) ≤ failure) :
    finiteEventProbability sampling
        (laplaceBadEvent successes sampleCount target error) ≤ failure
